title: Add `athena revert` that keeps records and gates on history and tests
summary: Add a supported `athena revert <job>` command. It reverts only the landed job's governed content and leaves its records (athena-gate's append-only records) in place. Before pushing it runs the full history check and the restored tests, and it refuses if either fails. The audience is the maintainer, who today reverts by hand and trips the history check. Tests cover the two cases named in the request.

defaults_applied.how: The command and tests are Rust.
New unit and integration tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check records kept and refusal on failing tests by running the tests, not that the code exists.
Refusal is enforced in code, before the push, and tested.
Behavior criteria are runnable with cargo test, run, clippy and fmt --check.
One focused command, with no changes to the history check rules.
A decisions entry and docs are written for an outside reader.
The fix is a supported path that keeps records. It does not add exempt entries for each revert.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Revert means: revert the job's governed content (the non-records paths of its landing commit), then re-add any records the plain revert would have deleted. Records stay append-only: new records may be added but none removed or edited.

The command is a new `athena revert` CLI subcommand in athena-cli, with the logic in athena-core (near manage.rs and land.rs). It reuses `check_history` from athena-gate and the existing tool-running path for tests.
Evidence for the problem: docs/decisions.md D111 says a revert deletes records and fails the history check. The 02837e0 revert in athena.toml was done by hand.
'Restored tests' means the test suite (cargo test) run on the tree as it will be after the revert, before any push.
Push is only attempted after both checks pass. Tests use the fake or local git and a local remote, as landing_tests.rs and the lifecycle tests do, and no network.
A design note is not needed beyond a decisions.md entry and a README or CHANGELOG line.

acceptance_criteria.text: A test reverts a landed job in a temp repository. Afterwards the job's records files still exist unchanged in HEAD, the job's content is gone, and `check_history` reports no violations. Run `cargo test --locked` and check the new test passes.

A test makes the restored tests fail after the revert (a content revert that breaks a test). The revert command returns an error naming the failing tests, and nothing is pushed or committed. The remote ref and local HEAD are unchanged. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A test where the history check would report a violation makes the revert refuse before pushing. Run `cargo test --locked`.
A control test shows that a plain `git revert` of the same landing does delete records and fails the history check. This shows the new command differs from it.
`cargo run -- revert --help` shows the subcommand with its job argument and a description. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
The revert code runs the history check and the tests before the push step, in that order, and the push is unreachable when either fails. The code shows this ordering.

docs/decisions.md gets an entry with the case, the decision, the alternatives (such as a plain git revert with an exempt entry), and the reversal cost. README or CHANGELOG mention `athena revert` with a one-line usage.
athena.toml and defaults.toml are unchanged. The command does not add `[history] exempt` entries.

out_of_scope: Moving records to the athena/records branch (D111 design) or changing the history check rules.
Adding [history] exempt entries or editing athena.toml or defaults.toml.
Reverting hand-made, non-Athena commits or multi-job squash merges.
Automatic re-landing of the reverted job.
departures: The cost and time are higher than the reference because this adds a new command and needs git-based integration tests. It touches landing and the history check, and the first cold cargo test build is slow. I also lowered the pass probability for the same reason.
hard_reason: It touches landing and the history check, which enforce the append-only records, so a mistake is costly and hard to see.
